description: Fish & Wildlife Management looks at how wildlife and fisheries are conserved: the problems they face, how the public helps, management practices in your state, a hands-on habitat project, wildlife observation and records, studying fish, and careers in conservation.

versions.label: Checked against official scouting.org excerpts (partial verification)

provenance.notes: Requirement numbering and topics were checked against excerpts of official Scouting America pages (scouting.org) returned by a search index on 2026-10-24. The pages themselves could not be opened from the build environment, so wording was not compared word for word and some sub-items may be summarized from partial excerpts. Summaries are ScoutPath's own words.

references.label: Official merit badge page (scouting.org Merit Badge Hub)

requirements.title: Conservation and management
requirements.summary: The goals of fish and wildlife conservation and management.

requirements.title: Problems facing wildlife
requirements.summary: Major problems facing fish and wildlife resources in your state.

requirements.title: How everyone can help
requirements.summary: Ways the public can contribute to conservation.

requirements.title: Management practices
requirements.summary: Management practices used by your state’s fish and wildlife managers.

requirements.title: A habitat project
requirements.summary: One option, such as nest boxes, bird feeders, a fishery or backyard habitat project, or a wildlife blind.

requirements.title: Wildlife records
requirements.summary: One option: observing and logging species, studying your state’s species of concern, or a wildlife scrapbook.

requirements.title: Studying fish
requirements.summary: One option, such as aging fish from scales, a creel census, or keeping an aquarium.

requirements.title: Careers
requirements.summary: Careers in fish and wildlife management and researching one of them.
